mainTopic: The end of אותו ואת בנו, and the opening of פרק כסוי הדם: the scope of the מצוה and why מוקדשין are exempt.
overview: This amud first closes the chapter אותו ואת בנו. רבי reads "יום אחד" as "a special day" that needs a כרוז. This is the source for a seller's duty to tell the buyer about related animals on four times a year. After the הדרן, a new chapter opens with a משנה on כסוי הדם. It applies everywhere and at all times, to חולין but not מוקדשין, and to חיה and עוף. The doubtful כוי gets its blood covered, but it may not be slaughtered on יום טוב. The גמרא then asks why מוקדשין are exempt. It first suggests רבי זירא's rule that covering needs earth below and above, which is impossible on the מזבח. When challenged that earth could still go on top, it answers with רבי זירא's rule that a step which could never be done holds back the whole מצוה. Finally, asked why the blood isn't scraped off and covered elsewhere, the גמרא says the משנה is about קדשי בדק הבית. That answer is examined further on the next amud.

steps.title: A special day needs an announcement
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads "יום אחד" as "a special day" and derives that on four times a year a seller must tell the buyer about the animal's mother or offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: "One day" means a special day, and a special day needs an announcement. From here they said: on four times in the year, someone who sells an animal to his friend must let him know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a source from the פסוק for the rule in the earlier משנה. On four special times of the year, a seller must tell the buyer that he already sold the mother or the offspring for slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אחד ("one") is read as מיוחד ("special, singled out"). On those special days, many people buy animals to slaughter right away. So the danger of slaughtering a mother and its child on the same day is high, and the Torah's wording hints that a warning is needed. That warning is the כרוז, which in practice means the seller informing the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: A special, singled-out day
An announcement or public notice
Requires, needs
Four set times of the year
To inform him

steps.whatToRemember: The duty to inform the buyer on four times a year has a source in the פסוק: "יום אחד" is read as "a special day that needs a כרוז."

phrases.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says:
"One day":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:28, the פסוק about not slaughtering a mother and its young on one day.

phrases.english: a special day requires an announcement,
from here they said:
on four occasions in the year
phrases.notes: These are the four times listed in the earlier משנה of this chapter.

phrases.english: one who sells an animal to his fellow must inform him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous part of the daf about the four times of year when the seller must inform the buyer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "יום אחד" means a special day, which needs a כרוז. This is the source for the seller's duty to inform the buyer on the four occasions.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing אותו ואת בנו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the chapter אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, אותו ואת בנו.
steps.whatsHappening: This line simply closes the chapter about not slaughtering a mother and its offspring on the same day. Nothing new is argued here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a traditional farewell said at the end of every chapter. It expresses the hope that we will come back and learn this chapter again. It marks a clear break before a new topic begins.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the chapter-closing formula
"It and its offspring": the name of the chapter that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you,
[chapter] "It and Its Offspring."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after רבי's final teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter אותו ואת בנו is complete. A new chapter begins next.

steps.title: Where, when, and to what covering the blood applies
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה sets the scope of כסוי הדם: everywhere and at all times, for חולין but not מוקדשין, and for חיה and עוף whether tame or wild.
steps.simpleTranslation: Covering the blood applies in ארץ ישראל and outside it, when the בית המקדש stands and when it does not, to non-sacred animals but not to sacrificial ones. It applies to wild animals and birds, both those kept at home and those that are not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens. The משנה lists all the situations where the מצוה of covering the blood after slaughter applies, and one situation where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה is tied to the person's body and the act of slaughter, not to the land. So it applies outside ארץ ישראל and even without the בית המקדש. The one limit given is חולין versus מוקדשין: sacrificial animals are excluded. The משנה also stresses that it does not matter whether the חיה or עוף was already at hand or had to be hunted.

keyTerms.meaning: Covering the blood after slaughtering a חיה or עוף
In the time when the בית המקדש stands
Non-sacred, ordinary animals
Animals set aside as קרבנות
An undomesticated (wild) animal
Readily available, already in one's possession

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה lists only חיה and עוף. A regular domesticated בהמה, like a cow or sheep, does not need כסוי הדם.
steps.whyThisMatters: The exclusion of מוקדשין becomes the first question the גמרא asks: why are sacrificial birds and animals exempt?

phrases.english: MISHNA: Covering the blood
applies in the Land [of Israel] and outside the Land,
in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple,
with non-sacred animals but not with sacrificial ones,
and it applies to an undomesticated animal and to a bird,
to one that is readily available and to one that is not readily available,
phrases.notes: Whether the animal was already at home or had to be hunted in the wild.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כִּסּוּי הַדָּם נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a brand-new chapter and topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כסוי הדם applies everywhere and at all times, to חולין but not מוקדשין, and to חיה and עוף, tame or wild.

steps.title: The doubtful כוי and slaughtering it on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Because a כוי is a ספק, we cover its blood. But we may not slaughter it on יום טוב, and if someone did, we do not cover its blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It applies to a כוי, because it is a doubt. And one may not slaughter it on יום טוב, and if one slaughtered it, one does not cover its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a special case: the כוי, an animal that may be a חיה or may be a בהמה. On a weekday we cover its blood to be safe. On יום טוב the rules change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the כוי might be a חיה, we cover its blood out of doubt. On יום טוב, covering blood involves handling earth, which is normally a forbidden מלאכה. It is allowed only for a definite obligation, not a doubtful one. So we do not slaughter a כוי on יום טוב at all, and if it was slaughtered, we leave the blood uncovered rather than do a forbidden act for a doubtful מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status as חיה or בהמה is uncertain
A doubt, uncertainty
A Festival day
And if he slaughtered it, after the fact

steps.whatToRemember: A כוי gets its blood covered only out of doubt. Because of that doubt, on יום טוב we neither slaughter it nor cover its blood.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that covering the כוי's blood proves it is a חיה. We cover it only because it might be one, and that is exactly why we don't cover it on יום טוב.

phrases.english: and it applies to a koy,
because it is a doubt.
phrases.notes: We don't know if it counts as a wild animal or a domestic one.

phrases.english: And one may not slaughter it on a Festival,
and if one slaughtered it,
one does not cover its blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's list to a doubtful case and gives a special יום טוב rule for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We cover a כוי's blood because of the doubt. But we may not slaughter it on יום טוב, and if it was slaughtered then, its blood is not covered.

steps.title: Why is the blood of consecrated birds not covered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's rule that כסוי הדם does not apply to מוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Consecrated birds: what is the reason their blood is not covered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the new משנה by asking why its blood-covering rule leaves out מוקדשין. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said כסוי הדם applies to חולין but not to מוקדשין, without giving a reason. The גמרא wants to know what makes קדשים different, since a bird offering is still a bird.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that explains the משנה
What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA
Consecrated [birds]: what is the reason [their blood is] not [covered]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה introduced in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason מוקדשין are exempt from כסוי הדם.

steps.title: Suggested answer: רבי זירא requires earth below and above
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason may come from רבי זירא, who learns from the word 'בעפר' that earth must be placed both under and over the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of רבי זירא's teaching: רבי זירא said that one who slaughters must put earth below and earth above. The verse says 'he shall pour out its blood and cover it בעפר.' It does not say 'עפר' but 'בעפר' (in earth), which teaches that earth must be below and above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, using the word אילימא ('if you say'), which hints this answer may not hold up. It brings רבי זירא's rule that covering needs earth both underneath and on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא reads the extra letter ב in 'בעפר' as 'inside earth,' so the blood must sit between two layers. If that is required, then any place where earth cannot go under the blood would not allow proper covering. The next step will apply this to the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say...': a suggested answer that may be rejected later
Earth below and earth above the blood
'In earth': the word רבי זירא uses for his teaching
This teaches

phrases.english: If you say it is because of [the teaching] of Rabbi Zeira,
as Rabbi Zeira said:
One who slaughters must place
earth below and earth above,
as it is stated: "And he shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth"
"earth" is not stated, but rather "in earth",
which teaches that one who slaughters must place
earth below and earth above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Maybe מוקדשין are exempt because proper covering needs earth below and above, which may not be possible for them.

steps.title: Putting earth under the blood would mean adding to the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: On the מזבח you cannot put earth under the blood: if the earth is made a permanent part of the מזבח, that adds to its structure, which the פסוק forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is not possible. How should he do it? Should he put down earth and make it a permanent part of the מזבח? Then he is adding to the structure, and it is written: 'All this is in writing from the hand of ה׳, which He made me understand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי זירא's rule cannot work for a bird offering whose blood goes on the מזבח. It tests the first option: making the earth a permanent part of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan of the מקדש was given exactly by ה׳, so nobody may add to the מזבח. Making earth a permanent part of the מזבח would be such an addition, so this option is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible
And make it a permanent part of something else (here, the מזבח)
Adding to the structure (of the מזבח)

phrases.english: And here it is not possible,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means a bird offering, whose blood is put on the מזבח.

phrases.english: how should he do it?
Should he place [earth] and nullify it [to the altar]?
He would be adding to the structure,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב מִיַּד ה׳ עָלַי הִשְׂכִּיל״.
phrases.english: and it is written: "All is in writing from the hand of the Lord, which He made me understand."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 28:19. The plan of the מקדש was set by ה׳, so it may not be changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי זירא's rule to the מזבח and rejects the first way of doing it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Making the earth a permanent part of the מזבח is forbidden as adding to its structure.

steps.title: If the earth is not made part of the מזבח, it blocks the blood
steps.stepSummary: The other option, leaving the earth separate, fails too, because then the earth is a barrier between the blood and the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not make it part of the מזבח, then it is a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes off the second option. If the earth stays separate, it stands between the blood and the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of an offering must touch the מזבח itself. Earth that is not part of the מזבח would be a חציצה, a barrier, so the blood would not be properly placed. Both options fail, so earth cannot go under the blood here.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrier that separates two things that must touch

steps.whatToRemember: Earth below the blood is impossible on the מזבח: as a permanent part it adds to the מזבח, and as a separate layer it is a חציצה.

phrases.english: Should he not nullify it?
Then it is an interposition.
phrases.notes: The earth would come between the blood and the מזבח, and the blood has to touch the מזבח directly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second option, completing the explanation that earth below is impossible.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Earth left separate from the מזבח is a חציצה, so it cannot be used either.

steps.title: Even if earth cannot go below, why not cover from above?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: even if earth cannot go under the blood, it can go on top, so covering should still be required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, below is not possible. But above is possible, so let him cover!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the רבי זירא answer. It argues that the earth above can still be done, so the blood should still be covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer explained only why earth below is impossible. The challenge says that missing one part should not cancel the whole מצוה: put earth on top and cover. So רבי זירא's rule does not fully explain the exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that
Covering (of the blood)

phrases.english: Granted that below is not possible,
above is possible,
let him perform a covering!

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דִּלְמַטָּה לָא אֶפְשָׁר, לְמַעְלָה אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggested answer of steps 6-8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי זירא's rule explains why מוקדשין are exempt from covering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being unable to put earth below does not stop putting earth above, so covering should still be required.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows covering from above is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its challenge with a ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן יוסף. If one slaughters a בהמה and then a חיה, he must cover the חיה's blood, even though that blood fell onto other blood with no earth underneath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: רבי יונתן בן יוסף says: If one slaughtered a חיה and afterward a בהמה, he is exempt from covering. If he slaughtered a בהמה and afterward a חיה, he is obligated to cover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for its question from step 9: covering only on top still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case, the חיה's blood lands on the בהמה's blood, so there is no earth under it. Even so, the ברייתא says he must cover it. That suggests earth on top alone is enough, so קרבן birds should need covering too.

keyTerms.meaning: An undomesticated animal, like a deer. Its blood must be covered.
A domesticated animal, like a cow. Its blood does not need covering.
Exempt, not obligated
Obligated

phrases.english: Wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef says:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט חַיָּה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט בְּהֵמָה –
phrases.english: If one slaughtered an undomesticated animal and afterward slaughtered a domesticated animal,
phrases.notes: The בהמה's blood lands on top of the חיה's blood, so the חיה's blood is already covered.

phrases.english: he is exempt from covering.
If he slaughtered a domesticated animal and afterward an undomesticated animal,
he is obligated to cover.
phrases.notes: Here the חיה's blood sits on the בהמה's blood with no earth under it, yet covering is still required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the challenge in step 9
steps.raayaObject: The claim that covering on top alone should be required
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן יוסף about a בהמה slaughtered before a חיה

steps.title: If earth underneath was possible, missing it is not a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with another rule of רבי זירא. When a step could have been done, leaving it out does not ruin the מצוה. When it could never be done, the whole thing fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי זירא, as רבי זירא said: Whatever is fit for mixing, mixing does not hold it back. Whatever is not fit for mixing, mixing does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof by using רבי זירא's rule about mixing flour and oil in a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בהמה-then-חיה case, he could have put earth down before slaughtering the חיה, so missing earth underneath does not cancel the מצוה. On the מזבח, earth underneath is never possible. Because of that, the מצוה of כסוי הדם does not apply there at all, even on top.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing flour with oil in a מנחה
Fit, possible to be done
Holds back, essential. Without it the whole thing is invalid.
A flour offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is a general principle: a step that is truly impossible can cancel a מצוה entirely, while a step that was merely skipped does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread the rule. It is the case where the step was NOT possible that becomes invalid, not the case where it was possible.

phrases.english: It is in accordance with Rabbi Zeira,
phrases.notes: This is a different statement of רבי זירא from the one in step 6.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Zeira said:
Whatever is fit for mixing,
phrases.notes: He is talking about a מנחה, where the flour is supposed to be mixed with oil.

phrases.english: mixing does not hold it back;
and whatever is not fit for mixing,
mixing holds it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and proof of steps 9 and 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between what was possible and what was impossible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covering on top alone is enough, so קרבן birds need covering
steps.terutzMaskana: Covering on top alone works only where earth underneath was possible. On the מזבח it never is, so there is no מצוה.

steps.title: Why not scrape the blood off and cover it elsewhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the blood can't be scraped off the מזבח and covered in another place. It proves from a משנה that scraped-up blood must be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him scrape it off and cover it! Didn't we learn in a משנה: blood that spurted, and blood that is on the knife, must be covered? So we see that one scrapes it up and covers it. Here too, let us scrape it up and cover it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Even if the blood can't be covered on the מזבח, it could be moved and covered somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says spurted blood and blood on the knife must be covered. That shows blood can be moved and covered away from where it fell. So the reason given in steps 6 to 11 should not be enough to exempt קרבן birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrapes off
Blood that spurted out to the side
Evidently, so we see
Here too

phrases.english: But let him scrape it off and cover it!
Didn't we learn in a משנה:
Blood that spurted, and blood that is on the knife,
one is obligated to cover it?
Evidently, one scrapes it up and covers it.
Here too, let us scrape it up and cover it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation that ended in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that blood on the מזבח cannot be covered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows blood can be scraped up and covered somewhere else, so the problem on the מזבח can be avoided.

steps.title: The משנה is about birds given for Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that blood of קדשי מזבח would be scraped up and covered. It explains that the משנה is really talking about קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were talking about קדשי מזבח, indeed so. Here, what are we dealing with? With קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge for altar offerings. It answers by saying the משנה refers to a different kind of holy animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קדשי מזבח, the גמרא now agrees that the blood is scraped off and covered. The משנה's exemption is moved to birds given to the בית המקדש fund for upkeep. This changes how the whole משנה is understood.

keyTerms.meaning: Things set aside to be brought on the מזבח as קרבנות
Things given to the בית המקדש fund for repairs and upkeep
Indeed so, that's right
What case are we dealing with?

steps.whatToRemember: At this point, the גמרא explains the משנה's exemption as being about קדשי בדק הבית, not altar offerings. Blood of altar offerings would be scraped off and covered. The discussion of this answer continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: If it were dealing with items consecrated for the altar,
indeed so,
phrases.notes: He means: yes, then we would scrape the blood off and cover it.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
With items consecrated for Temple maintenance.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה exempts altar offerings from covering
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about קדשי בדק הבית. Blood of altar offerings is scraped off and covered.
